FAQ
Q: Is Nanit a medical device?
A: No. Nanit is not a medical device and is not intended to diagnose, treat, monitor or prevent any medical condition, including SIDS. Always follow recommended safe sleep practices.
Q: Is the Australian model different to the US or UK version?
A: The camera itself is identical to the global Nanit Pro. Australian units ship with an AU power adapter, a warranty backed locally, and are supported directly by the Coolkidz Melbourne team on (lodge a request instead).
Q: Does Nanit work without Wi-Fi?
A: The camera keeps recording and working on the local network if the internet drops, so you can still see and hear your baby at home. Remote viewing, alerts and Nanit Insights resume once you reconnect.
Q: How does Nanit track breathing without touching my baby?
A: The camera reads the pattern on Nanit Breathing Wear, a swaddle, sleeping bag or pyjama with a printed pattern on the front. Nothing is worn on the body and no sensors touch the baby.
Q: Do I need to buy Breathing Wear separately?
A: Yes, breathing motion monitoring needs at least one piece of compatible Breathing Wear. Most complete Nanit systems include one to start, and more sizes can be bought as the baby grows.
Q: What is the difference between Nanit and a wearable sock monitor?
A: Wearable monitors clip a sensor to the baby's foot to estimate heart rate and oxygen. Nanit instead reads breathing motion from above using the camera and the Breathing Wear pattern, with nothing attached to the baby's body.
Q: Does Nanit need a subscription to work?
A: No. Live HD video, two-way audio, breathing motion monitoring and instant alerts all work without a plan. Nanit Insights adds sleep analytics, extended video history and personalised guidance, and is included free with every camera for the first 3 months.
Q: What happens after my 3 months of Nanit Insights ends?
A: The camera, live view, alerts and breathing motion monitoring keep working exactly as before. You can continue Nanit Insights on a paid plan to keep sleep analytics and extended video history, or keep using the core features at no extra cost.
Q: What does NextNap do?
A: NextNap predicts a baby's next nap window from their own sleep data, instead of a generic age-based schedule. It needs an active Nanit Insights plan and a compatible camera.
Q: Can more than one person use the app?
A: Yes. Other caregivers, such as a partner, grandparent or nanny, can be invited to the Parenting Team so everyone can view the camera and, on higher Insights plans, see sleep and care history.
Q: Do I need to drill for the Wall Mount?
A: Yes, the Wall Mount fixes above the cot for the cleanest, most permanent view and needs two wall anchors. The Floor Stand and Flex Stand need no drilling at all.
Q: Which setup do most Australian parents choose?
A: Pro + Floor Stand is the most chosen configuration: no drilling, works in a nursery or a rental, and moves with you if you rearrange the room.
Q: My camera won't connect to Wi-Fi, what should I try first?
A: Confirm the home network is 2.4GHz (Nanit does not connect to 5GHz-only networks), move the camera within range of the router during setup, and restart both the camera and router before trying again. If it still won't connect, use the support portal for step-by-step help.
Q: How much does shipping cost?
A: Standard shipping is free on orders of $200 or more, and a flat $12.95 under that. Express shipping is a flat $15. New Zealand ships for a flat $20.
Q: How long does delivery take?
A: Orders dispatch from the Melbourne warehouse within 1 to 2 business days. From there, most capital cities receive their order in 1 to 3 business days; Perth typically takes 4 to 7 business days.
Q: What is your returns policy?
A: 30 days from the date of delivery to return an item, provided it is unused and in its original packaging. Start a return through the support portal.
Q: How do I start a warranty claim?
A: Nanit Baby Monitor cameras carry a 2-year Australian warranty; every other product carries 1 year. Start a claim through the support portal or call the Melbourne team on (lodge a request instead), and they will confirm whether a repair, replacement or refund applies.

Magic.facts:
RANGE
Majestic: Entry point. Fixed-height, compact drop-and-turn mechanism. 20L capacity, holds approx. 25 nappies. 24 × 52cm (W×H). From $119.95. Ships with a bag roll and dispenser included. No 2nd-life bathroom lid available. 7 colourways.
Thoth: Slimline. Telescopic drop-and-turn, same height as Heka but a 24cm slimline footprint — built for tighter nurseries and bathrooms. 28L capacity, holds approx. 35 nappies. 24 × 63cm (W×H). From $149.95. Ships with a bag roll and dispenser included. 2nd-life bathroom lid available, $34.95. 6 colourways.
Heka L: Flagship. Telescopic and wide-bodied for maximum capacity. 40L capacity, holds approx. 45 nappies. 28.5 × 63cm (W×H). From $149.95. Ships with bin only. 2nd-life bathroom lid available, $34.95. 7 colourways.
shared_mechanism: All three ranges use the same wave-seal, drop-and-turn mechanism and work with any standard bin liner, or Magic's own bag for a guaranteed seal. Nothing about how the seal works changes between ranges — the difference is size, footprint and price.
material: 100% recycled polypropylene (PP), GRS-traceable material, across the whole range.
nappy_capacity_caveat: Nappy capacity depends on nappy size — the figures above are approximate, based on newborn/infant sizing. Expect fewer nappies per bin as the baby (and their nappies) grow.

CHOOSING
If floor space isn't a constraint and maximum capacity matters most (fewer bag changes), Heka L is the biggest. For a tight bathroom or nursery, Thoth has the same telescopic height as Heka but a slimmer 24cm footprint. For the lowest entry price and a compact fixed-height bin, Majestic is the starter option, though it doesn't have the 2nd-life bathroom lid.

ACCESSORIES
Bathroom lid accessory ($34.95) converts a Heka or Thoth base into a regular household bin once nappies are done — not available for Majestic. Magic's own nappy bags are designed for a guaranteed seal on any Magic bin and can help lock in odour for up to two weeks when used correctly.

HOW IT WORKS
Drop the nappy through the top opening — no bag threading, no touching the waste. Turn the lid to seal the wave seal shut behind it, locking odour into the chamber below. When the bag is full, use the small release button, turn and lift the top section off together with the bag, twist the bag a few times to seal it, then slide it out and dispose as usual.

CARE
Unscrew the drum holder and remove the round drum. Hand-wash all parts in lukewarm water with a few tablespoons of baking soda and a little mild soap. Don't put any part in the dishwasher — rinse and air-dry fully before reassembling.

TROUBLESHOOTING
smells: Check three things in order: the liner is free of holes and installed correctly (use a standard bag or an official Magic bag — thinner supermarket bags may not seal properly), the lid is closed fully after every use, and the bin is left in stand-by position (cup open, not rounded-side-up).
wont_open: Use the small release button to release the top. Turn it and lift the top section off together with the bag, then twist the bag a few times to seal it before sliding it out.

POLICIES

FAQ
Q: Is the NoseFrida suitable for newborns?
A: Yes, suitable from birth. The tube sits against the outside of the nostril, never inside, and the parent controls the suction. Use saline drops first and suction gently. If a newborn has persistent congestion, difficulty breathing or a fever, see a GP or child health nurse.
Q: Will I get mucus in my mouth?
A: No. A disposable hygiene filter sits between the collection chamber and the mouthpiece and is designed to stop mucus travelling toward the mouth. Replace the filter after every use.
Q: How do I use it?
A: 1. Insert a fresh filter. 2. Saline drops in each nostril, wait 20 to 30 seconds. 3. Rest the blue tube against the outside of the nostril to make a seal. 4. Breathe in gently through the red mouthpiece with a small circular motion. 5. Repeat on the other side. 6. Disassemble, bin the filter, wash the parts (top rack dishwasher safe; clear tube with 70% isopropyl alcohol). Full guide: /blogs/baby-care-guides/how-to-use-the-nosefrida-the-complete-australian-guide
Q: How often can I use it?
A: As often as needed, typically before feeds and before sleep during a cold. It is non-invasive and parent-controlled. Congestion lasting more than ten days, or with fever or breathing difficulty, needs a GP.
Q: How often do I replace filters?
A: After every use. Filters are single-use for hygiene and suction. Replacement packs of 20: /products/frida-baby-nosefrida-filters
Q: My baby cries when I use it. Am I doing it wrong?
A: Almost certainly not. Crying is normal, it is an unusual sensation rather than a painful one. A second person holding baby's arms helps. It stops as soon as you finish.
Q: What is the MediFrida?
A: A dummy-shaped medicine dispenser. Measure the dose into the syringe, attach it to the dummy, and press slowly as baby sucks so the liquid goes to the side of the cheek. Follow the dose your pharmacist or doctor gives. /products/frida-baby-medifrida
Q: What is the Flake Fixer for?
A: Cradle cap. Three steps in the bath: lather with the sponge, loosen with the silicone brush, lift flakes with the fine-tooth comb. A couple of times a week. If the scalp is red, weeping or not improving, see a GP or child health nurse.
Q: What is in the SnipperClipper Set?
A: Baby nail clippers with a safety guard and built-in magnifier, plus a nail file, for very small fingers and toes.
Q: When do I start dental care?
A: The Fingerbrush is for gums and first teeth from birth. The ToothHugger is a triple-sided toothbrush for toddlers. Australian dental guidance is to start brushing when the first tooth appears.
Q: Which kit should I buy?
A: Packing a hospital bag and want everything in one order: the Labour & Delivery Kit (includes gown, socks, carry bag and peri bottle). Already have a gown and want recovery items for home: the Postpartum Recovery Kit (no peri bottle or gown). Buying both together gets 10% off the Recovery Kit in cart.
Q: Are the kits suitable after a caesarean?
A: Yes. Lochia (postpartum bleeding) happens after every birth, so the peri bottle, ice pads, liners and underwear are all still relevant. For an incision, add the High Waist Disposable Underwear, which sits above the scar (/products/frida-mom-disposable-high-waist-underwear). Guide: /blogs/postpartum-guides/c-section-recovery-in-australia-what-to-expect-in-the-first-six-weeks
Q: How do the ice pads work?
A: Bend to activate, no freezer needed. Cooling comfort for the first 72 hours, and they are a full absorbent maternity pad as well. /products/frida-mom-instant-ice-maxi-pads
Q: How do I use the foam and liners?
A: Place a witch hazel cooling liner along your maternity pad, add one pump of Perineal Foam on top, replace with every pad change. Cooling comfort for perineal swelling and postpartum haemorrhoids.
Q: Why a peri bottle?
A: Rinsing with warm water after every toilet visit instead of wiping in the first weeks. The upside-down angled nozzle reaches without contortion. Useful after vaginal and caesarean births. /products/frida-mom-peri-bottle
Q: Boyshort or high waist?
A: Boyshort suits vaginal birth recovery. High waist sits above a caesarean incision. Both are soft, stretchy and disposable, and hold pads in place.

A: Baby Bunting stocks Frida Baby and Frida Mom in around 75 stores nationally, plus independents such as Bubs n Grubs, Baby Kingdom, Baby Village, Kiddie Country, Babyroad and HoneyBaby. Full list by state: /pages/stockists

Q: If the power is turned off , does the sleeptrainer remember it’s settings?
A: When the power shuts off, the sleeptrainer will not remember it’s settings unless batteries are inserted. We therefore advise to insert the batteries as back up in case power shuts off.
Q: How can I stop my child from playing with buttons and changing the settings?
A: The clock will enter key lock mode automatically after 1 minute. To manually activate the key lock: press the key lock button for 3 seconds. After activating the sleeptimer/wake-up time the key-lock is activated straight away, so that the settings cannot be changed anymore.
Q: Can I separate the wake-up time from the alarm time?
A: Yes, when setting the naptime or wake-up time, you can separately set the alarm. So you can set the sound alarm at a later time than the opening of the eyes.
Q: Can I switch off the orange screen, half an hour before wake-up?
A: It is not possible to switch off or change the time it turns on. The time is fixed at 30 minutes. If your child is still sleeping, the orange light will not wake him/her up. But if he/she does wake up, she knows straight away that it is not much longer by seeing the screen is orange.
Q: How can I close Sam’s or Davy’s eyes?
A: In the menu you select a time that Sam/Davy will automatically close their eyes every day. If you want to close them earlier you can press the DOWN button for 3 seconds and the eyes will close.
Q: How can I see if the clock is key-locked?
A: In the top of the LCD screen the key-lock symbol will appear when it is activated.
Q: How do I know if my clock is activated?
A: Sam or Davy is always activated. Once you have set the bedtime and OK to wake up time, he will automatically go to sleep every night and wake up every morning at the preset time.
Q: What if Sam is just not listening at all?
A: Try resetting Sam by pushing the tiny button with a paperclip on the bottom of the clock. This will usually make him listen.
Q: Sometimes the buttons do not react when I press them. What is wrong?
A: Probably the key lock has been activated. To unlock press the keylock-button, right, for 3 sec.
Q: If I do not want the alarm to sound, do I need to change the volume in the settings menu?
A: No, that is not necessary. In the menu (alarm clock icon) you can switch the alarm ON/OFF.
Q: Is there a demo function to show my child the working of Sam?
A: Yes there is a demo function in the settings menu. This demo will go through the entire bedtime ritual in around 20 seconds with preset time, so not the actual time that you have entered. You can check out our how to video for the demo function
Q: How long can I use the sleeptrainer when using batteries?
A: When using batteries, make sure you are using good alkaline batteries. Also we advise you to limit the nightlight to 5 minutes and select lowest brightness in the settings menu. Only then batteries will last around 4 weeks with normal use. With other settings the battery life will be decreased significantly.
Q: I can’t find the off function in the naptimer menu, what can I do?
A: You have to set the naptimer each time you want to use it, so there is not an off function in the menu because it ends automatically.
Q: Is it possible to set two wake up times so we can use a different wake up time for the weekends?
A: No, this is not possible.
Q: What kind of adapter do I need for Sam/Davy?
A: We advise you to use a 5V,1A adapter.
Q: How can I turn on the light?
A: Press the big round ON/OFF button on the bottom.
Q: How do I switch on/off the timer for the nightlight?
A: You can set the 60-minute timer by pressing the small clock and alarm button at the same time. Pam flashes once green when the timer is switched on and red if the timer is switched off.
Q: Can I change the settings for orange and green light?
A: This is not possible. The preset times can not be adjusted.
Q: How do I switch on the wireless connection?
A: Press the clock and triangle button at the same time. The wireless speaker symbol will appear in the display if activated. In the bluetooth menu of your phone, look for ZAZU-PAM and connect.
Q: How long does the wireless speaker stay connected?
A: If you use Pam with the timer, the bluetooth will switch off together with the light. If you use Pam without the timer, the connection stays as long as you are playing music/songs.
Q: Why do I need to reconnect to the wireless speaker?
A: If Pam needs to ‘look’ for connection 24/7 it takes up too much battery.
Q: How do I change the colour of the nightlight?
A: Press the big round button several times to get to your preferred colour.
Q: How do I change the brightness of the nightlight?
A: Switch on the nightlight by pressing the big button, then keep the big button pressed. The brightness will change. Let go at the right brightness. Pam will remember this setting for next use.
Q: How do I use Pam as a nightlight only?
A: Press the triangle button on the bottom for 3 seconds. In the display will appear a crossed out alarm clock. This means that the sleeptraining function is switched off.
Q: What kind of adaptor do I need to use for charging?
A: You can use any 5Volt output adapter for charging. Most telephone adapters comply with this.
Q: HOW DOES THE CRY SENSOR WORK?
A: The cry sensor operates by listening to sounds, such as crying. When it detects a certain level of sound, typically crying, it will activate the rocking. FAQ
Q: What is MiaMily?
A: MiaMily is a Swiss-designed travel and family lifestyle brand founded in 2014 by parents Alessandro Cereda and Cecilia Tsai. It is best known for ride-on luggage: hard-shell suitcases with a patented built-in seat that a child rides on while a parent pulls. In Australia the range is distributed exclusively by Coolkidz Australia.
Q: Where are MiaMily products designed and made?
A: All MiaMily products are designed in Switzerland and responsibly assembled in China, with materials, durability and safety standards overseen by MiaMily.
Q: What makes MiaMily luggage different from a normal suitcase?
A: The built-in seat. It turns the suitcase into a ride-on for kids, a resting seat for adults, a stroller alternative in airports and a hook for your nappy bag. The seat supports up to 100 kg including luggage contents, so it stays useful from toddler to teenager to adult. You also get 360° spinner wheels, a TSA-approved lock, adjustable handle heights, a child safety belt on the Carry On, Check In and Plus models, and a durable polycarbonate hard shell.
Q: Is the ride-on seat safe for children?
A: Yes, within its limits. The luggage has an aluminium frame rated to 100 kg and a wider base for stability, and the Carry On, Check In, Carry On Plus and Check In Plus include a built-in safety belt to secure your child. Children must be able to sit unassisted and should always be supervised by an adult. Use it on flat surfaces only, never on escalators or stairs.
Q: What age can a child ride on MiaMily luggage?
A: MiaMily does not set a minimum age; the rule is that the child must be able to sit unassisted, be belted in, and be supervised. Most families use the ride-on from the toddler years. The 100 kg capacity means older kids and adults can sit on it too.
Q: Does the Carry On Pro have a ride-on seat?
A: The Carry On Pro has a reinforced Sit Ready shell that supports up to 100 kg, so you can sit on it at the gate. It does not include the child seatbelt or the seat-back bag hook of the Carry On, Check In and Plus models, so it suits older kids, teens and adults rather than toddlers.
Q: Can I use the seat as a high chair?
A: The Carry On Plus is designed so the built-in seat doubles as a high chair on the go, with the wheel brake keeping the case still while your child is seated. Always belt your child in and stay with them.
Q: What happens to the seat when I travel without a child?
A: It becomes a bag holder. Hook or stack a nappy bag, tote or briefcase on the seat, or sit on it yourself during long waits.
Q: What are the dimensions and weight of the Carry On?
A: Carry On: 51 × 38 × 29 cm including wheels (20 × 14.9 × 11.4 inches), 4.3 kg, 43 litres. It is the same footprint MiaMily describes as fitting most airline overhead compartments.
Q: What are the dimensions and weight of the Check In?
A: Check In: 66 × 45 × 31 cm including wheels (25.9 × 17.7 × 12.2 inches), 6.5 kg, 77 litres.
Q: Can I bring MiaMily luggage on a plane as cabin baggage?
A: The Carry On size is designed to fit in most airline overhead compartments. Airline cabin policies and weight limits vary, particularly on Australian domestic carriers, so we recommend confirming your carrier's dimensions before flying. The Check In and Check In Plus are checked luggage.
Q: What are the dimensions of the Plus and Pro models?
A: Carry On Plus: 51 × 39 × 30 cm, 4.8 kg, 43 litres. Check In Plus: 65.5 × 46 × 33 cm, 5.9 kg, 77 litres. Carry On Pro: 51 × 39 × 23 cm, 3.5 kg, 48 litres, the lightest and slimmest of the range because it has no ride-on seat mechanism. Figures are as published by MiaMily.
Q: How big is the Expandable Backpack?
A: 44 × 31 × 11 cm, expanding to 22 cm deep. That takes it from 15 litres to 30 litres. It is made from 100% recycled polyester with YKK zips and has 11 pockets, including a laptop pocket, a thermal bottle pocket and an anti-theft passport pocket.
Q: How do I set the TSA lock?
A: Your luggage comes preset to 000. Shift the pin inside the lock from A to B, set your new three-digit code, then move the pin back to A. The lock is TSA-approved and does not come with a key; TSA agents can open it with a universal key if inspection is required.
Q: What is the luggage made of?
A: The suitcases use a polycarbonate hard shell with an anti-scratch texture, a polypropylene built-in seat and a polyester interior lining. The Expandable Backpack is 100% recycled polyester.
Q: How do I clean it?
A: Wipe the shell with a soft damp cloth and mild soap. Avoid solvents and abrasive cleaners, which can dull the textured finish. Let the interior lining air dry fully before packing.
Q: Where does MiaMily Australia ship?
A: We ship the entire range Australia-wide. Carry On luggage and Backpacks also ship to New Zealand. Every order is dispatched fast from the Coolkidz warehouse in Melbourne.

Q: Is Mamave safe to use during pregnancy?
A: Yes. every Mamave formula is designed to be pregnancy-safe. Products are developed by a cosmetic chemist who understands pregnancy skin, and avoid retinoids, parabens and synthetic fragrance. If you have specific medical concerns, we always recommend checking with your healthcare professional.
Q: Can I use Mamave products on my newborn?
A: The Bubba range is formulated for babies and young children: pH-balanced for baby skin, with gentle coconut-based cleansers and calming botanicals like calendula, aloe vera and chamomile. One range, head to toe.
Q: Is ‘natural’ skincare the same as pregnancy-safe?
A: No. and that's why Mamave exists. Natural doesn't automatically mean safe for pregnancy or for newborn skin. Mamave goes beyond traditional natural skincare: each product is developed using cosmetic science to support delicate skin at every stage, from pregnancy through to newborn care.
Q: Which skincare ingredients should I avoid while pregnant?
A: The ingredients most commonly avoided during pregnancy are retinoids (vitamin A derivatives), parabens and synthetic fragrance. Every Mamave formula leaves all three out, so you never have to decode a label. And if you're unsure about a product from another brand, your healthcare professional can advise.
Q: Why does my skin change during pregnancy?
A: Hormones. As they shift, skin can become drier, tighter, itchier and more reactive than usual. Hormonal breakouts and new sensitivities are common. That's why pregnancy skincare should be gentler and more supportive than your usual routine, not just the same products with a different label.
Q: Can I use Mamave if I have sensitive skin?
A: Mamave is designed for delicate, reactive skin. Pregnancy skin is sensitive skin. Formulas avoid synthetic fragrance and harsh additives, and many customers use the range on children with sensitive skin. As with any skincare, patch test first and check with your healthcare professional if you have a diagnosed skin condition.
Q: What age can I start using the Bubba range?
A: From newborn. The Bubba range is formulated for newborns, babies and young children: gentle, pH-balanced care for delicate new skin, from the very first bath onward.
Q: What helps protect against nappy rash?
A: Bubba's Barrier Cream. Apply a thick layer to your baby's bottom or other rash-affected areas. Its zinc oxide formula creates a breathable barrier between a wet nappy and delicate skin, protecting against moisture and irritation from rubbing.
Q: What can I use for cradle cap?
A: Bubba's Massage Oil is formulated to gently support cradle cap care. Warm a small amount in your hands and massage gently. Its plant-derived oils with calendula and aloe vera soften and soothe delicate skin.
Q: How do I massage my baby?
A: Warm a small amount of Bubba's Massage Oil by rubbing your hands together, then massage gently into your baby's skin, paying careful attention to their tummy, legs and arms. Daily massage is a beautiful way to turn everyday care into a calming ritual for both of you.
Q: Do I need separate hair and body products for my baby?
A: No. Bubba's Wash is a gentle all-in-one for hair and body. Coconut-based surfactants cleanse mildly, calming calendula soothes, and it's pH-balanced for baby skin. One product, head to toe, every bath.

Q: What happens when my child outgrows it?
A: Pass it on to a sibling, a friend, or the second-hand market, where the transferable warranty keeps it genuinely useful. If it's truly at the end of its life, it's 100% recyclable by the end user.
Q: What warranty does it come with?
A: A 2-year warranty from the original purchase date, honoured in Australia by Coolkidz Australia, the exclusive authorised distributor. It covers manufacturing faults under normal use, for original and second-hand owners with proof of purchase.
Q: How do I make a warranty claim?
A: Lodge a ticket at help.coolkidz.com.au with your proof of purchase, a description of the issue and photos or video. Approved claims are repaired, replaced, refunded or credited.
Q: Who sells Hannie in Australia?
A: Hannie is sold online at hannie.com.au and distributed exclusively by Coolkidz Australia Pty Ltd (Braeside, VIC), the family behind UPPAbaby, Frida, Nanit and other premium baby brands in Australia. Retailers can apply to become a stockist via the Coolkidz support portal.
Q: Is a chair-mounted seat as safe as a freestanding high chair?
A: Used correctly, yes. Chair-mounted seats have their own dedicated safety standard, EN 16120, covering the attachment system, restraint and stability, and the Hannie is tested to it (plus AS/NZS 8124.3). The two rules that matter everywhere: a sturdy four-legged chair underneath, and the harness clipped every time.

A: Plain boosters generally suit children from around 12 months who can sit confidently unaided, as they add height rather than support. The Hannie covers that stage too: its Toddler Seat mode is a booster rated to 25 kg, but it starts earlier, from around 6 months, with cushion and harness.

A: Rarely. Most fabric or clip-style travel seats hold your child at the table edge and rely on the table itself. The Hannie packs almost as small but includes a food-safe, dishwasher-safe tray, so your child has their own surface anywhere.
Q: Which seat is best for a small apartment?
A: A chair-mounted seat wins on floor space: it uses a dining chair you already own and packs to about 2 kg in a tote, so there's no bulky frame to park in a corner. A traditional high chair suits homes with room to leave it standing.

articles.title: Zazu sleep trainers Sam and Davy: common questions
articles.text:
Help with the buttons, eyes, wake-up settings and batteries on Sam the Lamb and Davy the Dog, plus the manuals and quick-start videos.
Buttons and key lock
The buttons do not react when I press them. What is wrong?
The key lock is probably on. To unlock, press the key lock button on the right for 3 seconds.
The key lock turns on automatically when the buttons have not been touched for 1 minute. This stops the settings being changed by accident.
How can I stop my child playing with the buttons and changing the settings?
The clock enters key lock mode automatically after 1 minute. To turn it on yourself, press the key lock button for 3 seconds.
When you start the sleep timer or wake-up time, the key lock turns on straight away so the settings cannot be changed.
Eyes and wake-up time
How can I close Sam's or Davy's eyes?
In the menu, choose the time Sam or Davy will close their eyes each day. To close them earlier, press the DOWN button for 3 seconds.
How do I open Sam's or Davy's eyes manually?
Unlock the device first, then hold the UP button for 3 seconds.
Can I switch off the orange screen that comes on half an hour before wake-up?
No. It cannot be switched off and the timing is fixed at 30 minutes.
If your child is still asleep, the orange light will not wake them. If they do wake, the orange screen tells them it is not much longer until wake-up time.
Can I separate the wake-up time from the alarm time?
Yes. When you set the nap time or wake-up time, you can set the alarm separately. This lets the sound alarm go off later than the eyes open.
Power and batteries
My sleep trainer does not work on batteries.
Use new alkaline batteries from a known brand, and change to a fresh set to be sure they are full. Some batteries, such as zinc-carbon batteries, do not have enough power to move the eyes.
My sleep trainer keeps resetting by itself.
The batteries are the most likely cause. Make sure they are not nearly empty, and do not use zinc-carbon batteries, which are made for low-power products. Use new alkaline batteries from a good brand.
If the power goes off, does the sleep trainer remember its settings?
Only if batteries are fitted. We suggest keeping batteries in the sleep trainer as a backup in case the power goes off.

How long should I use my teether for?
For as long as your child is teething. Clean it regularly.

articles.title: Using and cleaning your NoseFrida
articles.text:
The NoseFrida is a nasal aspirator you can use from birth. You create the suction yourself by breathing in through the mouthpiece, so you can feel the resistance and adjust it straight away. This guide covers how to use it, how to clean it and when to change the filter.
Before you start
Put a new hygiene filter into the filter chamber. The filter sits between the collection chamber and the mouthpiece and keeps mucus away from you.
Apply saline first. Put two to three drops in each nostril, then wait 20 to 30 seconds.
How to use it
Rest the large tube against the outside of one nostril so it forms a seal. The tube does not go inside the nose.
Breathe in steadily through the mouthpiece for two to three seconds while moving the tube in a small circle.
Repeat, then swap to the other nostril.
Many parents find it most helpful before feeds, before sleep and first thing in the morning.
Cleaning
After each session, throw the used filter away. Wash the parts in warm soapy water, or put them on the top rack of the dishwasher.
Filters
The NoseFrida itself is reusable. The filters are single use.
Use a fresh filter every time and bin it afterwards.
If suction feels weak, check the filter. A used or missing filter reduces suction.
Four filters come in the box. Replacement filters are sold separately in packs of 20. Use genuine Frida filters, which are sized for the NoseFrida chamber.
You may go through several filters in a day, so it helps to keep a spare pack in the change bag.
If you are worried about your baby
This article only explains how to use and clean the product. If you have any concerns about your baby's breathing, feeding or health, see your doctor or child health nurse.

The routine
Cleanse with the Peri Bottle. Fill it with warm water before you sit down. Hold it upside down and spray from front to back while you are on the toilet and afterwards, then pat dry.
Wear the disposable underwear. It holds a maxi pad and an ice pad in place. It is single use, so bin it after wearing.
Cool with an Instant Ice Maxi Pad. Fold the pad in half to activate it, then shake. Place it in your underwear and wear it for up to 20 minutes at a time. No freezer is needed. Each pad is single use.
Add a Cooling Pad Liner. Lay a liner on top of your maternity pad, front to back. Replace it every time you change your pad.
Finish with Perineal Foam. Shake the bottle, then pump the foam onto your pad or liner. You can use it at every pad change.
Looking after the Peri Bottle
Rinse the bottle and let it air dry between uses. Refill it so it is ready for your next bathroom visit.
Choosing your underwear
The High Waist style has a waistband that sits above a caesarean incision.
The Boyshort style has a lower rise and feels more like everyday underwear.
Both styles are one size fits most.
Which kit has the Peri Bottle?
The Postpartum Recovery Kit does not include the Peri Bottle. The Hospital Labour and Delivery Kit does, along with a gown, socks and a carry bag. The bottle is also sold separately.

articles.title: Setting up and using your Hannie Portable High Chair

Check the dining chair first

Seat depth: 35 cm

Safety every time
Read the manual before first use and keep it handy.
Always fit the 3-point harness.
Check that both straps are tight before every meal.
Supervise your child during use and never leave them unattended.
Never use the seat freestanding on the floor, on a table, or in wet environments.
Folding and carrying
The seat folds flat and slips into the tote bag that comes with it. Packed, it weighs about 2 kg including the Reversible Cushion, and it fits under most stroller baskets.

articles.title: Setting up and using your Magic nappy bin
articles.text:
Magic nappy bins do not use refill cartridges. Every bin in the range works the same way: you drop the nappy in, turn the top, and a wave seal closes behind it. Here is how to set yours up and use it day to day.
Know your model
Heka M, Heka L and Thoth L are telescopic, so they can extend in height when you need more room.
Majestic is a fixed-height bin.
Fitting a bag (Heka and Thoth)
Lift the lid off and place a bag into the holder.
Tuck the top of the bag under the rim so the seal can close over it.
Put the lid back on until it clicks.
Every nappy change
On a Heka or Thoth, drop the nappy into the opening and turn the top. The drum moves the nappy into the sealed part of the bin. Always return the top to its resting position afterwards.
On a Majestic, drop the nappy into the opening, then turn the handle forward and back. Leave the bin in the stand-by position, with the cup open, so no smell escapes.
Making more room
On a Heka or Thoth, twist the base to extend the bin. You can collapse it again for storage or travel.
Changing the bag
Press the small button on the side to release the top. The top is designed to stay locked until you do this, even when the bag is full.
Lift the whole top section off together with the bag.
Twist the bag a few times to seal it, then remove it and put it out with your usual rubbish.
Fit a new bag.

articles.title: Cleaning and odour tips for your Magic nappy bin
articles.text:
When a Magic nappy bin is used correctly it should not let odours out. If yours has started to smell, the cause is usually the bag, the lid, or the position the bin is left in between changes. Work through these checks first.
Check the bag
Make sure the bag is fitted correctly and has no holes or tears.
Most plastic bags and standard bin liners will work, but better quality bags give better results.
Avoid very thin supermarket shopping bags, as they may not seal properly.
Magic nappy bags are made to fit the bin and are designed to help lock in odours for up to two weeks when used correctly.
Check the lid and position
Close the top lid properly after every use.
Leave the opening in the stand-by position, with the cup open and not with the rounded side facing up.
Check that the bin itself is closed securely.
How to clean your bin
Unscrew the drum holder, as shown in your manual, and take out the round drum.
Wash all parts by hand in lukewarm water with a few tablespoons of baking soda and a little mild soap.
Rinse everything well.
Let every part air dry completely before you put the bin back together.
Do not put any part of the bin in the dishwasher.
Bag safety
Keep plastic bags away from children, and store bag rolls somewhere locked or out of reach.
Still noticing a smell?
If the odour continues after these checks and a full clean, send us a request and our Melbourne team will help.

articles.title: Using Mamave Bubba products on your baby
articles.text:
The Mamave Bubba range is made for babies and young children. This guide covers what each product is and how to use it.
What is in the Bubba range
Bubba's Wash: an all-in-one wash for hair and body, so you only need one product at bath time. Pump a small amount into the bath and cleanse your baby's skin with a soft washcloth, or lather it over their body and hair with a soft sponge or your hands.
Bubba's Moisturiser: a daily cream. It works best after a bath while the skin is still slightly damp, but you can also apply it to dry skin. Massage it in gently using circular motions.
Bubba's Massage Oil: a light plant oil for baby massage. Warm a small amount between your hands, then massage gently into the tummy, legs and arms. Add more as needed.
Bubba's Barrier Cream: a fragrance free cream for nappy change time. Apply a thick layer to your baby's bottom so it forms a barrier between the wet nappy and their skin.
Using the moisturiser and oil together
If your baby's skin looks extra dry, apply Bubba's Moisturiser first, then follow with Bubba's Massage Oil.
When to start
On the product pages for Bubba's Moisturiser and Bubba's Massage Oil, Mamave recommends waiting until your baby is at least one month old before using skincare products, because newborn skin is very delicate in the first month.
Scent
Bubba's Moisturiser and Bubba's Massage Oil are lightly scented with lavender and ylang ylang essential oils. Bubba's Wash contains mandarin essential oil. Bubba's Barrier Cream has no fragrance.
Patch test first
Mamave suggests patch testing before you use any skincare product. If irritation occurs, stop using the product and see your doctor. If your baby has a diagnosed skin condition, check with your doctor before use.

articles.title: Using Mamave Mumma products in pregnancy and after birth
articles.text:
The Mamave Mumma range is designed for pregnancy and the months after birth. This guide covers what each product is and how to use it.
What is in the Mumma range
Mumma's Oil: a body oil. Warm a small amount between your hands, then massage it into your belly, thighs, hips and bottom in circular motions. You can apply it up to three times a day.
Mumma's Moisturiser: a daily body cream. Apply generously to your belly, thighs, hips and bottom and massage in circular motions until absorbed. You can use it up to three times a day.
Mumma's Scrub: an exfoliating body scrub. Take a small handful, massage it onto your body in gentle circular motions, then rinse with water.
Mumma's Soak: bath salts. Sprinkle a handful into your bath water and let it dissolve before you hop in.
Getting the most from the oil and moisturiser
Both are best applied after a shower or bath while your skin is still slightly damp. You can also apply them to dry skin. Mamave recommends using the two together.
After birth
You can keep using the whole Mumma range after your baby arrives. The products are made for adult skin, so you can also use them when you are not pregnant.
About stretch marks
Mamave is clear that nothing can completely prevent stretch marks, and it does not guarantee that its products will.
Scent
The Mumma range is lightly scented with lavender and frankincense essential oils.
Check if you are unsure
Mamave suggests patch testing first. For Mumma's Soak, ask your doctor about safe bath temperature and how long to bathe during pregnancy. If you are unsure about using any product while pregnant, check with your doctor or midwife. If irritation occurs, stop using the product and see your doctor.

articles.title: Using the ride-on seat on your MiaMily luggage
articles.text:
Your MiaMily suitcase has a built-in seat, so your child can ride while you pull. This guide covers who can ride and how to set the seat up safely.
Who can ride
MiaMily does not set a minimum age. Your child must be able to sit up without help.
The seat is rated to 100 kg in total , and that figure includes whatever is packed in the case. Older children and adults can sit on it too.
The Carry On, Check In, Carry On Plus and Check In Plus have a child safety belt. The Carry On Pro has a shell you can sit on but no child belt, so it suits older children, teens and adults.
Setting up the seat
Stop the case on a flat surface. On the Plus range, press the wheel brake first.
Lift the seat up from the shell until it locks upright.
Sit your child facing forward and fasten the safety belt snugly.
Hang your nappy bag or tote on the hook on the seat back, then raise the handle to a height that suits you.
On the Plus range, release the brake, then pull smoothly and stay beside your child.
Safety rules
Always use the belt and always supervise your child.
Use the seat on flat surfaces only.
Never use it on escalators, stairs, travelators or slopes.
Do not use the seat as a step.
When nobody is riding
The seat makes a handy shelf for a nappy bag, tote or briefcase. When you are finished, fold it flat against the shell.

articles.title: Setting the lock and caring for your MiaMily luggage
articles.text:
A few simple habits will keep your MiaMily luggage working well trip after trip. Here is how to set the combination lock, clean the case and get ready to fly.
Setting the lock code
Your case arrives with the code set to 000 . To choose your own:
Open the lock and find the small pin inside the lock housing.
Move the pin from A to B.
Dial your new three-digit code.
Move the pin back to A, then test the lock once before you pack.
The lock is TSA-approved and has no key. If your bag is chosen for inspection, security staff can open it with a universal key. Keep a note of your code somewhere other than the luggage tag.
Cleaning and storage
Wipe the hard shell with a soft, damp cloth and mild soap.
Avoid solvents and abrasive cleaners or pads, as they can dull the textured finish.
After a trip, check the wheels for hair and grit. A wheel that drags usually has something wrapped around it.
Let the lining air dry completely before you pack or store the case.
Store it with the seat folded flat and the handle down.
Before you fly
The Carry On measures 51 x 38 x 29 cm including wheels and weighs 4.3 kg empty. The Carry On Plus measures 51 x 39 x 30 cm and weighs 4.8 kg. Cabin size and weight limits differ between airlines, so check with your airline before you travel. The Check In and Check In Plus are checked luggage.
Warranty
MiaMily luggage bought in Australia from an authorised retailer comes with a Limited Lifetime Warranty for manufacturing defects in materials and workmanship. Normal wear and tear, cosmetic marks, misuse and airline handling damage are not covered. Keep your proof of purchase.

articles.title: Setting up your Nanit Pro camera
articles.text:
Every Nanit Pro system uses the same camera. What changes is the stand or mount that holds it above your baby's sleep space. This guide covers what you should find in the box and how each option goes together.
What is in the box
Nanit Pro camera
Your stand or mount
A newborn Breathing Band and newborn pyjamas
USB-C cable and Australian power adapter
Quick start guide
The Floor Stand and Wall Mount systems also include a Flex Stand for travel. The Wall Mount system includes wall anchors.
Setting up each stand
Floor Stand: freestanding, with no drilling and no tools. Adjust the height so the camera sits directly over the cot. Allow about 10 minutes.
Wall Mount: fixes to the wall above the cot and has a channel for the cable. You will need a drill and the two wall anchors. Allow about 15 minutes.
Flex Stand: no tools needed. The flexible neck wraps onto a bassinet rail, shelf or travel cot, and it folds flat into its pouch. Allow about 5 minutes.
Connecting to Wi-Fi
The camera needs a 2.4GHz home network. It will not connect to a network that is 5GHz only. If it will not connect:
Check that your network is 2.4GHz.
Move the camera within range of your router while you set it up.
Restart both the camera and the router, then try again.
Changing your setup later
Stands and mounts are sold separately, so you can add a different one later and keep using the same camera.

articles.title: Nanit subscription, Wi-Fi and warranty questions
articles.text:
Here are answers to the questions Nanit owners ask most often once the camera is up and running.
Do you need a subscription?
No. Live HD video, two-way audio and instant alerts work without a plan. Nanit Insights is the optional plan that adds sleep analytics, extended video history and personalised guidance. It is included free with every camera for the first 3 months. When that ends, the core features keep working, and you can choose whether to continue Insights on a paid plan.
What happens if the internet drops?
The camera keeps working on your local network, so you can still see and hear your baby at home. Remote viewing and alerts return once it reconnects.
How does breathing motion monitoring work?
The camera reads the printed pattern on Nanit Breathing Wear, so no sensors touch your baby. You need at least one piece of Breathing Wear, and larger sizes are sold separately as your baby grows. Nanit is not a medical device and is not intended to diagnose, treat, monitor or prevent any medical condition, including SIDS. Always follow recommended safe sleep practices.
Can other carers use the app?
Yes. You can invite a partner, grandparent or nanny to your Parenting Team so they can view the camera too.
Can the camera play sounds?
Yes. Nanit Pro has four built-in sounds: birds, white noise, wind and waves. In the app you can set a timer for 30 or 60 minutes, or leave the sound playing continuously.
What warranty applies?
Nanit products bought from an authorised Australian retailer have a 1-year limited warranty from the date of delivery. It does not cover misuse, accidental damage, unauthorised repair, damage from incorrect installation or mounting, or problems caused by your home Wi-Fi or internet connection. Your rights under the Australian Consumer Law also apply.

articles.title: Changing modes on your smarTrike as your child grows
articles.text:
Your smarTrike stroller trike is built to change with your child. The Wind and Wonder ranges both move through the same four modes, and you do not need tools for any of the changes. Each change can be reversed just as quickly.
The four modes
Stroller mode, from 6 months (Wonder max only). The seat is reclined, the harness is on, the canopy is up and the child handlebar is locked. You steer from the parent handle. The Wonder max is the only model suitable under 10 months, because its seat reclines to 140 degrees.
Trike mode, from about 10 months. Sit the seat upright and unlock the child handlebar. Your child holds on while you keep steering.
Training mode, from about 18 months. Clip the pedals on and fold the canopy away or take it off. Leave the parent handle attached so you can guide and take over when little legs get tired.
Free riding, from about 2 years. Release the parent handle, lift it off and stow the harness. The handle clicks back on if your child needs a push home.
Knowing when to move on
The ages are a guide only, and every child gets there at their own pace. Most toddlers start pushing the pedals between 18 months and 2 years, often one foot at a time or backwards at first. Steady pedalling usually comes between 2 and 3 years. Around ten minutes is a good practice session.
If your child gets frustrated or wants to hop off after a minute, they may not be ready for pedals yet. Go back a mode for a few weeks and try again later.
Move to free riding only once your child can pedal and brake on purpose. Until then, keep a hand on the parent handle.
Handy to know
The pedals are detachable. Keep them in the seat pocket when they are not in use.
Your smarTrike folds in every mode, including with the pedals on.

articles.title: Folding and everyday safety checks for your smarTrike
articles.text:
A few quick habits keep every outing on your smarTrike safe and simple. The safety features described here are those of the Wonder range, which is tested to stroller safety standards.
Six habits for every ride
Harness on, every time. Do up the five-point harness in stroller and trike modes, even for a very short walk. It is only stowed away for free riding.
Brake on whenever you stop. Press the rear brake once with your foot to lock it and once more to release it. Use it on flat ground as well as on slopes.
Recline only on the Wonder max. Always have the harness done up when the seat is reclined.
Keep a hand on the parent handle. Hold on until your child can pedal and brake on purpose, which is usually between 2 and 3 years.
Check the locks after every fold. Listen for both clicks when you open the trike, then push.
Register your product. This lets you be contacted about any safety updates.
The bumper bar
The safety bumper bar closes in front of your child and opens with a press, so there is no need to tug at it. You can remove it once your child is riding on their own.
Folding and unfolding
Folding takes about three seconds and needs no tools. Release the fold lock and fold the trike in one motion. It works in every mode, and you can leave the pedals on.
When you open it again, both locks should click into place. Check them before you put your child in and set off.
Steering with one hand
The parent handle turns the front wheel through a full 360 degrees, so you can steer with one hand, turn on the spot and even go backwards. The shock-absorbing front wheel helps smooth out footpaths and gravel.
